SIGMOID_OVERFLOW.name: OverflowError in _sigmoid() on extreme negative floats
SIGMOID_OVERFLOW.exact_failure_domain: x <= -709.782712893384 (float inputs at or below IEEE 754 math range limit where math.exp(-x) overflows)
SIGMOID_OVERFLOW.partial_failure_domain: Stating negative floats cause an overflow or testing a concrete value like -710.0 or -1000.0 without stating the boundary threshold
SIGMOID_OVERFLOW.safe_valid_domain: x > -709.782712893384 (any finite float above threshold, positive floats, 0.0, or -math.inf which returns 0.0)
SIGMOID_OVERFLOW.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming that all negative numbers crash, that 0.0 crashes, or that positive numbers crash

NORM_ZERO_DIV.name: ZeroDivisionError in interval/distance normalization when lower == upper bound
NORM_ZERO_DIV.exact_failure_domain: Normalizing value distance against degenerate bounds where lower == upper bound (or equal interval bounds)
NORM_ZERO_DIV.partial_failure_domain: Mentioning division by zero or equal values without specifying that the lower and upper bounds are identical
NORM_ZERO_DIV.safe_valid_domain: Normalizing with distinct bounds where upper != lower
NORM_ZERO_DIV.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming that any zero value or zero distance causes division by zero

NORM_NAN_PROPAGATE.name: NaN propagation and range contract violation on NaN or non-finite inputs
NORM_NAN_PROPAGATE.exact_failure_domain: Passing float('nan') or inputs whose difference evaluates to NaN (such as inf - inf), causing _distance_norm to return nan instead of None or a normalized float in [0, 1]
NORM_NAN_PROPAGATE.partial_failure_domain: Stating that NaN inputs return NaN or unexpected value
NORM_NAN_PROPAGATE.safe_valid_domain: Passing finite numbers or non-comparable types that trigger exception handling and return None
NORM_NAN_PROPAGATE.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming _distance_norm fails on all floating point numbers or valid bounds

TV_EQ_NONE.name: TypeError on TreeValue == None (or unsupported object comparison)
TV_EQ_NONE.exact_failure_domain: Evaluating equality between TreeValue and NoneType (or any object that is not int, str, bytes, or TreeValue)
TV_EQ_NONE.partial_failure_domain: Stating that comparing with None fails without identifying that __eq__ raises TypeError instead of returning False
TV_EQ_NONE.safe_valid_domain: Comparing TreeValue with int, str, bytes, or another TreeValue instance
TV_EQ_NONE.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming that comparing two TreeValue instances fails, or that equality comparisons in general are broken

TV_HASH_CONTRACT.name: Python hash contract violation (equal objects produce unequal hashes)
TV_HASH_CONTRACT.exact_failure_domain: TreeValue instances equal to primitive values (e.g. TreeValue(1) == 1 or equal coerced values) producing different hash values
TV_HASH_CONTRACT.partial_failure_domain: Noting that hash values differ or hashing is broken without specifying the equality contract violation (a == b but hash(a) != hash(b))
TV_HASH_CONTRACT.safe_valid_domain: Hashing standalone TreeValue objects or comparing identical TreeValue instances where hash matches
TV_HASH_CONTRACT.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming that TreeValue is unhashable or that hash() raises an unhandled exception

TV_TO_INT_VAL.name: FandangoConversionError / ValueError in to_int() on non-numeric bytes or strings
TV_TO_INT_VAL.exact_failure_domain: Calling to_int() on a TreeValue containing non-digit characters, empty bytes/strings, or non-numeric representations
TV_TO_INT_VAL.partial_failure_domain: Stating that to_int() fails on letters or testing a specific non-numeric string like 'abc'
TV_TO_INT_VAL.safe_valid_domain: Calling to_int() on TreeValue containing valid decimal digits (e.g. b'123', b'0', b'-5')
TV_TO_INT_VAL.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming to_int() fails on all inputs or cannot parse any byte sequence

TV_RADD_STR.name: ValueError / FandangoConversionError in __radd__ when prepending strings or bytes
TV_RADD_STR.exact_failure_domain: Evaluating expression 'prefix' + TreeValue or b'prefix' + TreeValue where TreeValue contains non-digit characters
TV_RADD_STR.partial_failure_domain: Stating that string concatenation with + fails or testing a concrete string like '' + tv
TV_RADD_STR.safe_valid_domain: Concatenating where TreeValue contains numeric digits, or appending TreeValue + 'suffix' where __add__ is used
TV_RADD_STR.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming that TreeValue cannot be used in any string operations

TV_ENCODING.name: LookupError in _str_to_bytes() on invalid or unknown codec string
TV_ENCODING.exact_failure_domain: Calling _str_to_bytes(value, encoding) with an empty string or unregistered codec name
TV_ENCODING.partial_failure_domain: Testing an invalid codec name without recognizing LookupError
TV_ENCODING.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming _str_to_bytes fails on all encodings or cannot encode strings

TV_DEEPCOPY_SHARED.name: Reference sharing of mutable _trailing_bits list in TreeValue.__deepcopy__
TV_DEEPCOPY_SHARED.exact_failure_domain: Invoking copy.deepcopy() on a TreeValue possessing trailing bits, which passes trailing_bits=self._trailing_bits directly without copying, causing the clone and original to share the identical mutable list instance
TV_DEEPCOPY_SHARED.partial_failure_domain: Noting that deepcopy does not isolate internal state or causes unintended cross-instance mutation
TV_DEEPCOPY_SHARED.safe_valid_domain: Calling copy.deepcopy() on TreeValue instances with no trailing bits or mutating distinct instances
TV_DEEPCOPY_SHARED.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming copy.deepcopy() crashes with an unhandled exception or that shallow copy fails

DT_TO_GRAMMAR_ASSERT.name: AssertionError or failure in to_grammar() on degenerate or malformed trees
DT_TO_GRAMMAR_ASSERT.exact_failure_domain: Invoking to_grammar() on a DerivationTree lacking proper production rules or degenerate structure
DT_TO_GRAMMAR_ASSERT.partial_failure_domain: Noting to_grammar crashes on specific trees without characterizing the missing production structure
DT_TO_GRAMMAR_ASSERT.safe_valid_domain: Invoking to_grammar() on complete, valid derivation trees with defined production expansions
DT_TO_GRAMMAR_ASSERT.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming to_grammar() fails on all derivation trees

DT_ROUNDTRIP.name: Structural or attribute loss during tree serialization/deserialization round-tripping
DT_ROUNDTRIP.exact_failure_domain: Serializing and deserializing DerivationTree where custom node attributes, sources, or parent links are dropped
DT_ROUNDTRIP.partial_failure_domain: Noting that tree attributes differ after round-trip without specifying which fields drift
DT_ROUNDTRIP.safe_valid_domain: Round-tripping trees with basic symbol and terminal children structures
DT_ROUNDTRIP.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming serialization always crashes or fails to execute

DT_REPR_CRASH.name: RecursionError in __repr__ on cyclic parent/child tree references
DT_REPR_CRASH.exact_failure_domain: Evaluating repr(tree) on a DerivationTree containing circular or recursive parent-child references
DT_REPR_CRASH.partial_failure_domain: Noting repr crashes on recursive structures without identifying maximum recursion depth limit
DT_REPR_CRASH.safe_valid_domain: Evaluating repr(tree) on standard directed acyclic trees
DT_REPR_CRASH.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming __repr__ crashes on all trees or deeply nested linear trees

DT_PREFIX_SLICE.name: AssertionError in prefix() on root nodes where parent is None
DT_PREFIX_SLICE.exact_failure_domain: Calling tree.prefix() on a root DerivationTree or tree where parent is None (assert ref_tree.parent is not None fails)
DT_PREFIX_SLICE.partial_failure_domain: Stating prefix() crashes on root nodes or prefix(0) fails
DT_PREFIX_SLICE.safe_valid_domain: Calling prefix() on intermediate subtrees that possess an active parent node
DT_PREFIX_SLICE.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming prefix() crashes on all subtrees

DT_CHILD_SLICE.name: IndexError on indexing unexpanded or empty children list
DT_CHILD_SLICE.exact_failure_domain: Accessing children[i] or removing children on non-terminal derivation trees with empty children
DT_CHILD_SLICE.partial_failure_domain: Testing an out-of-bounds child index on an empty tree
DT_CHILD_SLICE.safe_valid_domain: Accessing children within bounds on populated derivation trees
DT_CHILD_SLICE.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming children cannot be accessed or iterated

DT_SLICE_PARENT_HIJACK.name: Parent pointer corruption on child nodes during read-only tree slicing
DT_SLICE_PARENT_HIJACK.exact_failure_domain: Slicing a DerivationTree (tree[start:stop]) which constructs a SliceTree whose set_children() mutates child._parent = slice_tree on the original tree's nodes in-place, hijacking the parent reference and corrupting parent traversal
DT_SLICE_PARENT_HIJACK.partial_failure_domain: Noting that slicing a tree corrupts parent pointers or causes subsequent assertion failures in prefix()
DT_SLICE_PARENT_HIJACK.safe_valid_domain: Accessing children via single integer index (tree[i]) or operating on un-sliced derivation trees
DT_SLICE_PARENT_HIJACK.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming tree slicing raises an immediate exception or cannot create a slice

PARSE_EMPTY_CONSTRAINT.name: IndexError in parse() when constraints contains empty or whitespace strings
PARSE_EMPTY_CONSTRAINT.exact_failure_domain: Passing constraints=[''] or whitespace-only constraint strings (c.split()[0] crashes on index 0)
PARSE_EMPTY_CONSTRAINT.partial_failure_domain: Noting that parse crashes on empty constraint string without identifying the split()[0] indexing failure
PARSE_EMPTY_CONSTRAINT.safe_valid_domain: Passing valid non-empty constraint expressions (e.g. ['<start> == "a"']) or empty constraints list []
PARSE_EMPTY_CONSTRAINT.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming parse() crashes whenever constraints parameter is provided or on all empty strings

PARSE_LEXER_STALL.name: Lexer stall or freeze on escaped grammar delimiters
PARSE_LEXER_STALL.exact_failure_domain: Grammar specifications containing escaped delimiter tokens ('\|') causing catastrophic regex backtracking
PARSE_LEXER_STALL.partial_failure_domain: Stating that escaped pipe characters freeze or take excessive time to parse
PARSE_LEXER_STALL.safe_valid_domain: Grammar specifications with standard pipe '|' alternation and unescaped delimiters
PARSE_LEXER_STALL.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming the parser hangs on all complex grammars or alternation rules

PARSE_NAME_ERROR.name: FandangoValueError / NameError on unresolved grammar identifier
PARSE_NAME_ERROR.exact_failure_domain: Grammar specifications referencing undefined non-terminal rule names (leaking exception during symbol validation)
PARSE_NAME_ERROR.partial_failure_domain: Testing an undefined rule name like <undefined>
PARSE_NAME_ERROR.safe_valid_domain: Grammars where all non-terminals on the RHS have matching definitions on the LHS
PARSE_NAME_ERROR.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming the parser rejects valid non-terminal references

PARSE_SILENT_DROP.name: Silent dropping of constraints containing trailing comments or syntax
PARSE_SILENT_DROP.exact_failure_domain: Constraint strings with trailing comments ('# comment') being silently discarded without being enforced in population
PARSE_SILENT_DROP.partial_failure_domain: Noting that comments in constraints are dropped without verification
PARSE_SILENT_DROP.safe_valid_domain: Standard constraint strings without trailing comments
PARSE_SILENT_DROP.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming constraints are never enforced or always ignored

PARSE_DESC_RECUR.name: RecursionError in check_constraints_existence_children on recursive grammars with descendant constraints
PARSE_DESC_RECUR.exact_failure_domain: Evaluating descendant constraints (<start>..<target> or item searches) on recursive or mutually recursive production rules, where memoization occurs after recursive exploration, causing infinite recursion
PARSE_DESC_RECUR.partial_failure_domain: Noting that descendant constraints hang or exceed maximum recursion depth
PARSE_DESC_RECUR.safe_valid_domain: Evaluating constraints on non-recursive grammars or constraints without descendant search syntax
PARSE_DESC_RECUR.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming all constraints on recursive grammars crash or that parse cannot handle recursion

PARSE_EMPTY_FAN_FILES.name: IndexError on empty fan_files list when use_stdlib=False and constraints provided
PARSE_EMPTY_FAN_FILES.exact_failure_domain: Calling parse([], constraints=[...], use_stdlib=False) which attempts grammar = grammars[0] on an empty grammars list, raising uncaught IndexError: list index out of range
PARSE_EMPTY_FAN_FILES.partial_failure_domain: Stating that parse crashes on empty input files without specifying use_stdlib=False
PARSE_EMPTY_FAN_FILES.safe_valid_domain: Passing at least one grammar specification file or keeping use_stdlib=True
PARSE_EMPTY_FAN_FILES.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming parse fails on all empty specifications

DEF_EMPTY_RHS.name: FandangoSyntaxError on empty RHS string in generated definition grammar
DEF_EMPTY_RHS.exact_failure_domain: Calling make_def(lhs, '') with an empty string for rhs, producing an invalid grammar '<_lhs> ::= \n<lhs> ::= <_lhs>' that fails parsing
DEF_EMPTY_RHS.partial_failure_domain: Testing make_def with empty string without noting that the failure occurs during grammar parsing of the output
DEF_EMPTY_RHS.safe_valid_domain: Calling make_def(lhs, rhs) with non-empty rhs containing valid tokens or rules
DEF_EMPTY_RHS.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming make_def always raises SyntaxError or cannot create grammar definitions

DEF_UNICODE_CORRUPT.name: FandangoSyntaxError on non-ASCII Unicode identifiers in make_def LHS
DEF_UNICODE_CORRUPT.exact_failure_domain: Passing non-ASCII Unicode identifiers (e.g. Cyrillic, Kanji, or accented Latin) to make_def, producing grammars rejected by the ANTLR lexer
DEF_UNICODE_CORRUPT.partial_failure_domain: Testing a specific non-ASCII character in rule name
DEF_UNICODE_CORRUPT.safe_valid_domain: Passing standard ASCII alphanumeric identifiers (e.g. '<my_rule_123>') to make_def
DEF_UNICODE_CORRUPT.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming make_def rejects all rule names or valid ASCII identifier strings

DEF_HEX_OVERFLOW.name: Hex escape overflow / multi-byte corruption in make_def on characters with ord(c) > 255
DEF_HEX_OVERFLOW.exact_failure_domain: Passing non-Latin-1 characters with code points ord(c) > 255 (e.g. Euro sign '€', Greek, Cyrillic, CJK, or emoji) to make_def, causing f"b'\x{ord(c):02x}'" to format with 3+ hex digits (e.g. b'\x20ac') which Python evaluates as byte 0x20 followed by ASCII characters 'a' and 'c' (3 bytes), corrupting the character into an unintended multi-byte literal
DEF_HEX_OVERFLOW.partial_failure_domain: Stating that non-ASCII or high codepoint characters cause encoding issues or testing a concrete character like '€' without specifying the hex escape overflow mechanism
DEF_HEX_OVERFLOW.safe_valid_domain: Passing ASCII characters and Latin-1 characters within range ord(c) <= 255 (0 to 255) to make_def
DEF_HEX_OVERFLOW.overgeneralization_triggers: Claiming make_def cannot handle any non-printable characters or that all binary escapes fail
